note: Pre-registered before any bet or backtest (src/nflpred/qb_news.py). Hypothesis: the market takes time to fully price starting-QB news, so the side the news favors, bet at our books before the consensus spread has moved half a point, beats the closing line. Evidence so far is weak and must be proven live: in the news audit (history/news_audit.json, 2026 weeks 1-6) consensus spreads moved 0.58 pts on average in the 6 h after an AI QB signal vs 0.21 pts before, but QB calls were only 61% accurate (41 graded) and the average move after negative QB signals was -0.08 pts (direction unclear). This track uses only the strictest calls (certainty >= 0.9, full name matched to the Sleeper roster, source accuracy weight >= 0.9, news about the next game published after the team's previous game ended). Paper only; judged on closing line value with closing PRICES (spread_bets.closing_margins). Do not edit to fit results; bump the version.

qualify.roster: verify.roster == match on a Sleeper roster, player name has first and last name
qualify.starter: the game's projected starting QB on the dashboard (game['home_qb'] / game['away_qb'])
qualify.direction: starter unavailable or a backup named starter: bet AGAINST that team; starter cleared after being listed questionable/doubtful/out on the injury report: bet FOR that team
qualify.line_move: consensus home spread (median of sportsbooks) now vs our last odds snapshot at or before the news was first published/seen, measured toward the bet side
qualify.price: best spread at your books (my_books.json), most favorable point then price

checks: every hourly watch and every 15-minute QB-news check (qb_news_fast.yml); fresh odds are fetched only when a signal qualifies

grading.result: ATS at our point and price
grading.clv: our point and price valued at our own last pre-kickoff snapshot's price-implied margin (spread_bets.closing_margins)
